chunks: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥukaym, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام, concerning:

A woman experienced nifās, so she left the salat (prayer) for thirty days, then she became pure, then after that she saw blood. He said: “She leaves the salat (prayer), because her days—the days of purity—have passed together with the days of nifās.”

key_terms.الدَّمَ: blood seen after the initial postnatal period
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the obligatory salat (prayer) that is left during a state preventing worship
key_terms.الطُّهْرِ: ritual purity or the period of purity between bleedings
key_terms.تَطَهَّرَتْ: she became ritually pure from bleeding

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman sees blood again after thirty days of nifās and a period of purity?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a woman who experienced postnatal bleeding and then saw blood again after becoming pure. The Imam عليه السلام rules that she leaves the salat (prayer), based on the calculation of her days of purity having already elapsed alongside the days of nifās.
